source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public 13–15, 16:1–35 and 18 align directly. Public 16:36–50 maps to Hebrew 17:1–15; public 17:1–13 maps to Hebrew 17:16–28. All 214 original records, including every annotation, are hashed exactly. Later numbering differences require separate mapping.

key_decisions.decision: Distinguishes broader ancestral-house sanctuary liability from Aaron-and-sons priesthood liability; retains bearing guilt with note.
Preserves limits despite Levitical service and shared lethal liability, not only a penalty on the intruder.
Keeps joined service and restriction; unauthorized is a role category, not an ethnic foreigner.
Keeps difficult double gift direction: to priests for service, dedicated to LORD; does not silently change to from-LORD wording.
Preserves altar/inside-curtain scope, gift-service ambiguity in note and explicit execution sanction without generalizing unrestricted access.
Renders mishchah as allotted portion with anointing-linked alternate noted; preserves custody and gift dimensions.
Adopts as-most-holy construal rather than commanding meals in Holy of Holies; note records spatial alternate and priestly male scope.
Preserves explicit daughters and clean-household permission, contrasted with preceding male-only most-holy offerings.
Conveys herem as irrevocable dedication in this context, without making destruction its automatic meaning.
Retains womb-opening image and mandatory redemption for humans and unclean animals; no human sacrifice implication.
Keeps three clean animal groups exempt from redemption and distinguishes blood splashing from fat burning.
Retains daughters again, lasting provision and concrete covenant-of-salt image rather than substituting an explanation.
Preserves contrast between territorial share and LORD-as-inheritance, without denying later Levitical towns.
Retains death consequence and general Israelite access boundary in contrast with authorized Levites.
Keeps Levitical responsibility and no territorial inheritance; their offenses retains pronoun ambiguity with note.
Keeps conditional lack of guilt and final profanation/death warning, linking holiness and distribution rather than mere finances.
